findings.statement: Installation scope (any workspace vs. selected workspaces only) is chosen when the integration is created and can't be changed afterward; only 'any workspace' integrations are eligible for Marketplace listing.

findings.statement: Public integrations use OAuth 2.0 with a page picker: during authorization the user chooses which pages (or a provided template) to grant the integration access to.
Internal integrations are tied to a single workspace and use a static API token with no OAuth flow and no per-user authorization.
Capabilities - such as reading content, updating content, and inserting content - are set when creating the integration, rather than requested as individual OAuth scope strings.
On Enterprise-plan workspaces, an owner can restrict members to only pre-approved connections, meaning workspace members can only install connections a workspace owner has pre-approved.
Each user authorizes a public integration individually and gets their own access token scoped to their workspace; other members of the same workspace must complete their own authorization to use it.
Composio maintains a managed OAuth app for Notion by default; a custom Notion app is recommended mainly for production use, your own branding, custom scopes, or a dedicated rate limit.
Creating a public integration requires at least one redirect URI; an OAuth client ID and secret become available afterward from the Configuration tab.

Notion's full capability list is small and fixed: Read content, Update content, Insert content, Read comments, Insert comments, plus a single user-information access level chosen from No user information, User information without email addresses, or User information with email addresses.

claim.text: Creating a public integration and using it via OAuth is fully self-serve, with no partner program mentioned anywhere in the setup or publishing docs.
Neither Notion's integration-creation guide nor its Marketplace publishing guide describes any security review or assessment step.
Marketplace listing is explicitly optional - a public integration works through its OAuth flow for any number of workspaces without ever being listed or reviewed.
On Enterprise-plan workspaces, an owner can restrict members to only pre-approved connections.

tierReason.text: Marketplace listing is explicitly optional for Notion integrations - a public integration works through its own OAuth flow, for any number of workspaces, with no Notion review required at all.

scopeForks.text: If you want Marketplace/Integration Gallery listing (optional, for discoverability), the integration must be scoped to 'Any workspace' at creation and goes through a Notion team review that typically responds within 5-10 business days; a 'Selected workspaces only' integration is never eligible for listing, and switching requires creating a brand-new connection.

claim.text: Composio maintains a managed OAuth app for Notion by default, so a developer can skip registering their own.

whatYouLose.text: On a managed app, the consent screen shows the platform's name and brand instead of yours, and scopes/rate limits are typically fixed rather than something you control.

whenToSwitch.text: Switch to your own Notion integration once you need your own branding, specific capabilities, or a dedicated rate limit.

flow.text: A developer creates a public integration, sets its capabilities and installation scope, and each user authorizes it individually through Notion's OAuth flow with a page picker.

appTypes.text: Internal integrations use a static API token for one workspace with no OAuth; public integrations use OAuth 2.0 and can be installed by any user who authorizes them.

tokenNotes.text: Each user who authorizes a public integration gets their own access token, scoped to that user's workspace and page selections.
